title: A1 final test
intro: 20 questions drawn from the whole level. Explanations come at the end.

items.prompt: Nosotros ___ de Argentina.
items.explanation: Origin takes ser, and nosotros takes somos.
optionNotes: Estar is not used for where you are from.
Son is for ellos / ellas / ustedes.
Sois is for vosotros.

items.prompt: En mi calle ___ dos farmacias.
items.explanation: To say that something exists somewhere, use hay. It never changes for plural.
optionNotes: Están is for things already known: las farmacias están en mi calle.
Es does not say that something exists.
Tiene needs a subject (mi calle tiene dos farmacias). After en mi calle, use hay.

items.prompt: El sábado vamos ___ cine.
items.explanation: Ir a + el becomes al.
optionNotes: A + el (the article) joins into al.
Del means from the / of the.
With ir, the place takes a, not en.

items.prompt: La madre de mi padre es mi ___.
items.explanation: Your father's mother is your grandmother: abuela.
optionNotes: Tía is your aunt.
Prima is your cousin.
Sobrina is your niece.

items.prompt: You did not understand a shop assistant. What do you say?
items.explanation: ¿Puede repetir, por favor? asks someone (usted) to say it again.
optionNotes: This asks for the price.
This asks for the time.
This asks where the person is from.

items.prompt: Por la mañana no ___ tiempo para desayunar.
items.explanation: Tener is irregular: the yo form is tengo.
optionNotes: The yo form has a g: tengo.
Tiene is for él / ella / usted.
The yo form does not change e to ie.

items.text: Mi hermano {{1}} levanta a las ocho y yo {{2}} levanto a las siete.
items.explanation: Levantarse is reflexive: él se levanta, yo me levanto.
The adjective agrees with gatas (feminine plural): bonitas.
No goes straight before the verb.
Problema ends in -a but is masculine: el problema.

items.prompt: Which word is written correctly?
items.explanation: Te-LÉ-fo-no is stressed on the third syllable from the end, so it needs a written accent on the é.
optionNotes: Without the accent the stress would fall on -fo-.
A word has only one written accent.
The stress is on -lé-, not on the first syllable.

items.prompt: You speak to a hotel receptionist you don't know. Which word for “you”?
items.explanation: With a stranger in a formal situation, use usted.
optionNotes: Tú is for friends, family and people your age.
Vosotros is for a group.
Tu without an accent means “your”.

items.prompt: Mis hermanas y yo vivimos con ___ padres.
items.explanation: Padres is masculine plural: nuestros padres.
optionNotes: Padres is plural.
Padres is masculine.
Vuestros is for vosotros.

items.context: I work from Monday to Friday, in the morning.
items.text: Trabajo {{1}} lunes {{2}} viernes, por la mañana.
items.explanation: From … to … = de … a …: de lunes a viernes.
Colors come after the noun: una bicicleta roja.

items.prompt: Mis amigos ___ en una oficina.
items.explanation: Mis amigos = ellos: trabajan.
optionNotes: Trabaja is for one person.
Trabajamos is for nosotros.
Trabajáis is for vosotros.

items.prompt: ¿___ (tú) venir a mi casa el sábado?
items.explanation: Poder changes o → ue: puedes.
optionNotes: The stem changes o → ue: puedes.
Puede is for él, ella, usted.
Podemos is for nosotros.

items.prompt: Write the present tense of querer.
items.explanation: e → ie in every form except nosotros and vosotros: queremos.

items.prompt: Hoy no voy a clase porque ___ enfermo.
items.explanation: Being sick today is a state: estoy enfermo.
optionNotes: Ser would describe a lasting quality.
Tener needs a noun: tengo fiebre.
Hay means “there is”.

items.prompt: A mis padres ___ gusta viajar.
items.explanation: Mis padres = ellos: les gusta.
optionNotes: Le is for one person.
Se is reflexive.
Los is a direct object pronoun.

items.context: Tomorrow I'm going to visit my grandmother.
items.explanation: Voy a + infinitive: voy a visitar. Visitar + a person takes a: a mi abuela.

items.prompt: It is 10 p.m. and dark. You meet a neighbor. You say:
items.explanation: After dark, the greeting is buenas noches.
optionNotes: Buenos días is for the morning.
Buenas tardes is for the afternoon, until it gets dark.
Noche is feminine: buenas.

items.prompt: You want to know someone's job (to a friend):
items.explanation: ¿A qué te dedicas? asks about someone's job.
optionNotes: This is not a Spanish question.
This means “Which one are you?” (for example in a photo).
Trabajo is the yo form: “where do I work?”.

items.prompt: It's 4:45. In Spain people usually say:
items.explanation: A quarter to five: son las cinco menos cuarto.
optionNotes: That is 3:45.
From two o'clock on, the verb is son.
That is 5:15.

items.prompt: Mi cumpleaños es el 3 ___ marzo.
items.explanation: Dates: el + day + de + month: el 3 de marzo.

items.prompt: You want to know the total in a café. You ask:
items.explanation: For the total: ¿Cuánto es?
optionNotes: Cuántos asks “how many”.
¿Qué cuesta? is not used for a price.
That asks how much the other person has.

items.prompt: Which number is sesenta y siete?
items.explanation: Sesenta is 60 and siete is 7: 67.
optionNotes: 76 is setenta y seis.
57 is cincuenta y siete.
17 is diecisiete.

items.prompt: Trabajo ___ sábados. (on Saturdays, every week)
items.explanation: Every Saturday = los sábados, with no preposition.

items.prompt: Match each place with its meaning.
items.explanation: Watch out: la biblioteca is the library; la librería is a bookstore.

items.prompt: ¿Cuánto ___ estos tomates?
items.explanation: Estos tomates is plural: cuestan.
optionNotes: Cuesta is for one thing.
Costar changes o → ue: cuestan.
Cuestas is for tú.
